ai-at-work.title: When the Trump administration cracks down on Anthropic, who benefits?
ai-at-work.excerpt: On the new episode of Equity, we discussed what actually prompted the administration's latest moves against Anthropic, and what this might mean for the AI ecosystem.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: The Trump administration is apparently turning up the heat on Anthropic, the AI company behind Claude, prompting questions about what triggered the enforcement action and what it signals for the broader AI landscape. This matters to digital workplace folks because AI tools are rapidly becoming core infrastructure for knowledge work, and regulatory uncertainty creates real risks for companies betting on these platforms for productivity gains. Here's the thing though: every time government gets aggressive with one AI vendor, it usually just reshuffles the deck rather than slowing innovation, so don't expect your employees to stop pestering IT about AI access anytime soon.

ai-at-work.title: Trump kneecaps Anthropic, SpaceX bags Cursor and Databricks debuts AI agent coworker
ai-at-work.excerpt: Databricks may keep refusing to go public, but this week it wasn’t shy about proclaiming its intentions to be a central player in artificial intelligence. At its annual Data + AI conference in San Fra
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Databricks is positioning AI agents as the next enterprise system of record, essentially arguing these autonomous tools should become central to how companies operate. This matters because if AI agents actually deliver on the promise, they could fundamentally reshape how we think about digital workplace architecture and employee workflows. That said, I've heard "this will revolutionize everything" about fifteen different technologies over three decades, so I'll believe it when I see actual adoption numbers that aren't from the vendor's own case studies.

ai-at-work.title: Recovery speed becomes the new mandate in cyber resilience strategy
ai-at-work.excerpt: Cyberattacks are no longer just an information technology problem; they’ve become a board-level business continuity crisis, forcing enterprises to rethink cyber resilience strategy from the storage la
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Enterprises are shifting from "prevent attacks" thinking to "recover fast" thinking, making backup speed and resilience a board-level priority instead of leaving it to IT to sort out quietly. This matters because when your digital workplace goes down, recovery time directly impacts revenue, customer trust, and employee productivity, so it's no longer a technical afterthought. After 30 years watching IT get blamed for everything while working with shoestring budgets, I'm genuinely pleased to see executives finally understanding that a good backup strategy is worth more than all the prevention tools combined.

digital-culture.title: Free lunch! The oldest retention strategy is also one of the most effective
digital-culture.excerpt: Years ago when I was a professor, I brought a cohort of executive strategic design MBA students to Florence, Italy, to study the Renaissance as a living laboratory for business innovation. We visited
digital-culture.dwp_take: A Fast Company piece argues that free lunch remains one of the most effective employee retention strategies, drawing parallels to Renaissance workshops where communal meals and spaces fostered creativity and connection. For digital workplace professionals, this is a reminder that retention isn't solved by ping-pong tables and Slack integrations, it's solved by genuine human interaction and the simple act of people eating together. After thirty years watching companies throw money at software solutions while their teams sit isolated, I can tell you the studio director greeting people at the door beats most HR tech budgets combined.

digital-culture.title: Why most U.S. workers are checked out and bosses are the last to know
digital-culture.excerpt: Michael Scott, the hapless regional manager at the center of the American version of “The Office” played by Steve Carell, believed he was the world’s best boss. He even had the mug to prove it. Meanwh
digital-culture.dwp_take: A new study confirms what we already knew: most American workers are disengaged, and their managers have no clue it's happening. This matters because digital workplace leaders are often the ones tasked with fixing engagement through tools and platforms, when the real problem is sitting in the corner office ignoring the warning signs. The irony is that companies spend millions on collaboration software to solve a people problem that starts with bad management, which is like buying a fancy espresso machine to fix a broken kitchen.

industry-news.title: Apple Reportedly Preparing Second-Generation iPhone Air for Spring 2027
industry-news.excerpt: Apple’s next iPhone Air could arrive in spring 2027 with camera and battery upgrades as the company shifts toward staggered iPhone launches. The post Apple Reportedly Preparing Second-Generation iPhon
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple is planning a second-generation iPhone Air for spring 2027 with improved cameras and battery life, continuing its strategy of spreading out iPhone releases throughout the year instead of one big annual drop. For digital workplace teams, this matters because staggered device releases mean employees will be cycling through phone upgrades at different times, which impacts your mobile device management strategy and support load. Here's the reality though: most organizations won't see these phones in employee hands for another three years, so maybe let's focus on actually supporting the iPhones people are using today instead of planning for fictional ones.

industry-news.title: The Complete Guide to Gantt Charts: Examples & How to Use One
industry-news.excerpt: Learn how to manage projects by using a Gantt chart, and which industries and project types it would benefit most. Discover the history and key features with our guide. The post The Complete Guide to
industry-news.dwp_take: TechRepublic published a comprehensive guide on Gantt charts covering their history, key features, practical examples, and which industries benefit most from using them. This matters to digital workplace folks because project visibility is foundational to collaboration, and Gantt charts remain one of the most effective ways to keep distributed teams aligned on timelines and dependencies. Honestly, if your organization still isn't using Gantt charts by now, you're probably also still printing emails, and we need to talk.

industry-news.title: MSP 3.0: Managed services enter a new era
industry-news.excerpt: Automation, AI, and growing compliance demands are forcing MSPs to rethink their role, moving beyond traditional IT support towards a more strategic advisory model.
industry-news.dwp_take: Managed service providers are being pushed to evolve from basic IT support into strategic advisors, driven by automation, AI adoption, and tightening compliance requirements. This shift matters because your digital workplace infrastructure depends on MSPs who actually understand your business strategy instead of just fixing broken printers. Here's the thing though: half the MSPs out there will rebrand themselves as "strategic partners" without changing a single process, so don't fall for the marketing. Kick the tires and ask what they've actually automated in the last year.

industry-news.title: Legacy kit behind vast majority of cyber attacks on utilities
industry-news.excerpt: With equipment and software poorly suited to withstand modern cyber threats, organizations need to do more to identify unmanaged or vulnerable systems
industry-news.dwp_take: Utility companies are getting hammered by cyberattacks because they're still running ancient infrastructure that was never designed for today's threat landscape. This matters to digital workplace folks because it's a brutal reminder that your shiny new collaboration platform means nothing if the foundational systems keeping the lights on are held together with duct tape and prayers. The real kicker is that nobody wants to spend money replacing systems that technically still work, right up until the moment they don't and you're explaining to angry customers why their power went out.
